# OpenAI DevDay October 2025: Major Announcements

OpenAI held its third annual DevDay on October 6, 2025, at Fort Mason in San Francisco, drawing over 1,500 attendees. CEO Sam Altman delivered the opening keynote, with a fireside chat featuring Apple designer Jony Ive later in the day [2].

## ChatGPT as a Platform

The most significant strategic announcement was OpenAI's transformation of ChatGPT into an application platform resembling an operating system. A new **Apps SDK**, built on Model Context Protocol (MCP) as an open standard, allows third-party apps—including Spotify, Canva, Zillow, Figma, Booking.com, and Expedia—to integrate directly into ChatGPT with deep context and data-sharing capabilities [7]. This represents a deliberate shift away from raw model development toward making AI practically useful across all software [8]. The scale of the platform is notable: ChatGPT serves 800 million weekly active users, with 4 million developers processing 6 billion tokens per minute via the API [7].

## AgentKit and Developer Tooling

OpenAI launched **AgentKit**, a comprehensive toolkit for building, deploying, and monitoring AI agent workflows, complete with visual builders and evaluation tools [1]. Additional developer tools included **ChatKit** and **Codex**, the latter now generally available with a reported 10x increase in usage since August 2025 [1]. These tools collectively represent OpenAI's push to own the "agentic stack" for developers [8].

## Model Releases via API

On the model side, OpenAI made **GPT-5 Pro**, **gpt-realtime-mini**, and **Sora 2** available through the API [1]. GPT-5 Pro offers high-accuracy reasoning capabilities, while Sora 2 enables realistic text-to-video generation for developers to integrate into their own products [6]. However, these were largely broader rollouts of existing models rather than entirely new releases, consistent with OpenAI's pattern of launching major models outside of scheduled events [8].

Overall, DevDay 2025 signaled OpenAI's pivot from being a model provider to becoming the foundational layer for conversational software and agentic applications.
